reader.requirement: At --std 85 a CLOSE naming several relative (or mixed) files, each with or without WITH LOCK, must execute as a separate CLOSE for each file-name-1 in the written order: each file's own I-O status updated, each removed from the open mode, each WITH LOCK applied only to its own file, and a failing member (status 42) must not stop the later members.

edition-consulted.switches: CLOSE WITH LOCK admitted at 85 (removed at 2023, COBOL0902); the per-file series itself is edition-agnostic

reader.edition-search: grep for CLOSE in VersionConformancePass.cs and every BoundClose consumer; BindClose and EmitClose read ctx.Edition only to stamp a BoundRejected, never to switch behaviour
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the WITH LOCK phrase per file-name-1 is admitted at 85 and refused at 2023; the one-CLOSE-per-file series is the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf18_05 covers order, per-file status and reopen for plain CLOSE across all three relative access modes; not exercised: WITH LOCK on some members only, the same file named twice

probes.expected: CLOSE F1 WITH LOCK F2 F3 WITH LOCK = three CLOSEs: all 00, F1 and F3 locked (reopen 38), F2 reopens 00; CLOSE F2 F2 = 00 then 42; CLOSE after a failed OPEN = 42

probes.printed: error COBOL1693: CLOSE 'F2' with the REEL/UNIT phrase - the phrase may be used only with a sequential-organization file
probes.expected: the Relative I-O CLOSE format admits only WITH LOCK; REEL/NO REWIND on a relative file refused

probes.printed: error COBOL0902: the CLOSE WITH LOCK phrase was removed in COBOL-2023
probes.expected: later edition refuses WITH LOCK; 85 admits it

reader.notes: BindClose builds one BoundClose per file-name-1 and wraps them in BoundImplicitSeries, so each member is a whole CLOSE with its own status store and USE hook in source order. The mixed WITH LOCK probe shows the lock applies per member and the duplicate-name probe shows the second member sees the first one's result. The witness covers the order clause with a USE procedure.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-230/r1a.cob at --std 85 (relative seq/random/dynamic, FILE STATUS, one USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR on all three): CLOSE F1 F2 F3 with F1 unopened printed 'CL1 42 00 00 TR=U429999/' (USE runs after member 1 while F2,F3 still 99, later members still close); CLOSE F1 F2 WITH LOCK F3 WITH LOCK with F2 unopened printed 'CL2 00 42 00 TR=U004299/' (USE sees F1 already closed, F3 not yet); reopen F1 00, F3 38 (lock only on its own member). r1b.cob: 'CLOSE F1, F2 LOCK; F3 LOCK.' (LOCK without WITH, comma/semicolon separators) gives the same output. cite.py: OK  §1985:VIII.4.2.4 GR7  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR7.
